title: Yeast Questionnaire
field_body:
Candidiasis is an overgrowth of candida (yeast) in the GI tract and it can absolutely cause weight loss resistance and carbohydrate cravings. SIFO (Small Intestine Fungal Overgrowth), particularly when it's candida, not only is a barrier to weight loss, but it can lead to leaky gut, gastric ulcers, Crohn's and ulcerative colitis. 

Use this document to assess whether you likely have a yeast overgrowth. Of course for confirmation, we can run an integrated urinalysis panel as well.

title: *Chewing Food - Tips and Tricks and Reasoning Behind WHY it is so important
field_body:
The question was asked: Do you have any tips for chewing food?  I think I need to chew my food more.

Here's the ANSWER:

There is no EASY trick to chewing your food more. But here are some simple tips to help, and I provide the reasoning behind the "why" it is so important.

But:  As weird as it may sound, being mindful and appreciative of the amazing food you are chewing, swallowing and nourishing your body with will actually help your body synchronize with the food (at an energetic level, that scientists have not yet been able to explain). It allows your body to optimally take it in and utilize all the nutrients.  Think of putting 93 octane in a Ferrari or putting 87 in a Ferrari.  The car demands a cleaner fuel to operate at optimal performance. Your body is the same way.  You can get by on 87, but you won't look and feel and perform as well as we know you are capable of.

So here are some tips.

Chew Your Food – Don’t just chew enough to swallow. Your saliva plays a huge role in breaking down food. Take your time when eating. Start by chewing at least 30 times before swallowing.  

Sit Down – Sitting down can help relax you and aid good digestion.

Take Ten Deep Breaths – Taking a moment before eating will help put your body in the right state for good digestion.  Some people pray, depending on your religion or spiritual beliefs. It helps their bodies calm down and be thankful for the nourishment they are about to ingest.

Smell Your Food – The simple act of smelling your food will switch your salivary glands on and get your stomach ready for the meal you are about to enjoy.
